24 The diagram shows an experiment to produce a stationary wave in an air column. A tuning fork,
placed above the column, vibrates and produces a sound wave. The length of the air column can
be varied by altering the volume of the water in the tube.
tuning fork
air column
water
tap
The tube is filled and then water is allowed to run out of it. The first two stationary waves occur
when the air column lengths are 0.14 m and 0.42 m.
What is the wavelength of the sound wave?
A
0.14 m
B
0.28 m
C
0.42 m
D
0.56 m

hints: Notice the air column is open at the tuning fork and closed by water, so there is an antinode at the top and a node at the water surface.
Recall that successive resonances in a closed pipe occur at $\lambda/4$, $3\lambda/4$, $5\lambda/4$ and so on, so the distance moved between them is $\lambda/2$.
Calculate the change in air column length from $0.14\text{ m}$ to $0.42\text{ m}$ and double it to obtain the full wavelength $\lambda$.
walkthrough: Identify the pipe: the top near the tuning fork is open and the water surface is a closed end, so resonance lengths satisfy $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4$ and so on.
The first stationary wave at $L_1 = 0.14\text{ m}$ is the fundamental with $L_1 = \lambda/4$, and the next at $L_2 = 0.42\text{ m}$ has $L_2 = 3\lambda/4$.
Subtract to eliminate the end effect: $L_2 - L_1 = 3\lambda/4 - \lambda/4 = \lambda/2$.
Substitute values with units: $\lambda/2 = 0.42\text{ m} - 0.14\text{ m} = 0.28\text{ m}$.
Multiply by 2: $\lambda = 2 \times 0.28\text{ m} = 0.56\text{ m}$ with correct unit of length. This is option D.

A.explanation: 0.14 m is the length of the shortest air column, which is only one quarter of a wavelength for a pipe closed by water.

B.explanation: 0.28 m is the increase in length from $0.14\text{ m}$ to $0.42\text{ m}$, which equals half a wavelength, not a full wavelength.

C.explanation: 0.42 m is the length of the second air column, which is three quarters of a wavelength for a closed pipe.

D.explanation: The length increase of $0.28\text{ m}$ is $\lambda/2$, so $\lambda = 2 \times 0.28\text{ m} = 0.56\text{ m}$.
